action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

# RCA implementation versions: V1, V2, and V3 (combined v0.3)

This archive preserves the earlier prompt/rule implementations and packages the current V3 role implementations together for review.

This update corrects the multi-claim Evidence Worker handoff to HERA and adds a native local Ollama adapter for all three versions. See `CHANGELOG_v0.3.md` and `OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md`.

The V3 package now also includes `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py`, a closed-loop synthetic scenario runner that dispatches Assessor-approved outward requests, simulates a constrained fixture custodian response, re-ingests replies through PIRIS, and resumes V3 role processing. See the V3 README for scope and commands.

| Version | Label | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Prompt-only baseline | The original five-role baseline in the legacy codebase; select `config/experiments/v1_basic.yaml`. |
| V2 | Prompts plus methods/rules | The original research-inspired role methods and prompts; select `config/experiments/v2_full.yaml`. |
| V3 | Neurosymbolic-inspired prototype | Standalone CFERP Lead, SAHS Specialist, EWV3 Evidence Worker, HERA1 Assessor, PIRIS Intake, and an Intake-to-Lead runtime. |

## Layout

- `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/Original_V1_V2_Codebase.zip` is the supplied V1/V2 archive unchanged.
- `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/source/` is its extracted copy. The included `VERSION_GUIDE.md` maps the exact implementations and profiles. V1 and V2 share this versioned codebase and are selected by experiment profile; they are not falsely represented as separate source snapshots. The copy includes a runner-only `case_id` option so the bundled R3 fixture keeps its own case identity; the V1/V2 role implementations are unchanged.
- `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` contains the current role package source and selected tests. SAHS uses LLM proposal generation, typed causal representations, Python validation, and ASP/Clingo candidate composition. The other roles provide retrieval, assessment, coordination, and provenance functions; not every role independently uses a symbolic solver.
- `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/orchestration/v3_bridge.py` routes queued CFERP work to SAHS, EWV3, and HERA1. `v3_runtime.py` runs PIRIS for initial and later submissions, converts registered materials to CFERP records, and starts or refreshes Lead work. The host/operator still controls external request dispatch and human responses.

## Testing

Run tests from `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` after installing `requirements-sahs.txt` (Clingo is required for SAHS):

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements-sahs.txt
PYTHONPATH=. python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

The V3 label describes the architecture and implementation direction. It does not claim that every role independently uses a symbolic solver. Package and integration tests use scripted model responses; no OpenRouter live call is included in this archive.

## Live V1/V2/V3 run

The combined launcher runs the V1 prompt-only profile, V2 full profile, and V3 pipeline sequentially on the bundled staged R3 fixture. Run it from this directory:

```bash
python -m pip install -r V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/requirements-sahs.txt
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="your-key-in-your-shell"
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py --check-only
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py \
  --case V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/examples/r3_synthetic_case.json \
  --model nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free \
  --output outputs/r3_all_versions
```

The case materials are synthetic research fixtures, not authentic company records. The launcher saves separate V1/V2 and V3 outputs plus a combined status report. It is an exploratory workflow comparison, not a controlled causal-quality comparison: V1/V2 use a custodian/request loop, while V3 receives staged PIRIS material arrivals. The full V3 instructions are in `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/README.md`.

## Run against a local Ollama model

The archive includes a native Ollama `/api/chat` adapter. It uses only the Python standard library, sends JSON-mode requests, records local token/timing metadata, and never switches to fixture responses. Install and start Ollama separately, then pull a model supported by your machine:

```bash
ollama pull <model-tag>
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py \
  --provider ollama_native \
  --model <model-tag> \
  --base-url http://localhost:11434 \
  --check-only
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py \
  --provider ollama_native \
  --model <model-tag> \
  --base-url http://localhost:11434 \
  --output outputs/r3_ollama
```

Use the exact tag shown by `ollama list`; the preflight checks `/api/tags` before starting either pipeline. This runs V1, V2, and V3 through the native local API. No OpenRouter or OpenAI key is needed. See `OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md` for direct Python use, configuration, tests, and the distinction between native Ollama and the existing OpenAI-compatible Ollama endpoint.

content.text:
Not really. The pushed `README.md` is the one already in the folder: it covers the setup and run commands, but it wasn't written for someone landing on the public repo.

**What's useful in it**
- A table showing what V1, V2 and V3 each are.
- The layout of the folders.
- How to run the tests.
- How to run all three versions, through OpenRouter or a local Ollama model.

**What's wrong with it**
- **Out of date:** the title says "combined v0.3" and it points to `CHANGELOG_v0.3.md`, but the code is v0.4.
- **No introduction:** it opens with "This archive preserves…". Nothing says what the project is or what problem it studies.
- **Closed loop barely covered:** the five roles are only listed, never explained. Nothing describes how documents flow between them, and the ground truth and scoring aren't mentioned.
- **No results:** nothing on the gpt-oss runs or what we've learned so far, such as the answer reserve and the window size.
- **Missing links:** it doesn't point to `RESEARCH_BRIEF.md`, `CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md`, `FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md` or `FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md`.
- **Mentions files that aren't there:** it refers to `outputs/`, which isn't pushed.

A rewrite would start with a short introduction and a description of the five roles and how documents flow between them. It would keep the setup and run commands, and add how scoring against the ground truth works and where the results stand. It would also link the detailed docs and say plainly that the cases are synthetic and the run outputs aren't included.

Exit code 1
# v0.4 — Closed-loop synthetic scenario replay

- Added a V3 closed-loop runner that handles Lead-approved outbound request
  dispatch, fixture-bounded simulated custodian replies, PIRIS re-ingestion,
  and continuation of Specialist/Evidence Worker/Assessor processing.
- The simulated custodian can select only fixture item and request-slot IDs
  provided in its call. Python rejects unknown IDs and extra response fields.
- Non-selected documents continue as unrequested arrivals. A final no-match
  reply is explicitly labeled as a search limitation, not proof of absence.
- Output records the simulated response trace and states that no human was
  contacted. This remains a synthetic workflow simulation, not an authenticated
  R3 incident replay or a claim that the investigation reached a final RCA.
- Added unit coverage for response ID bounds and malformed custodian output.
# Research brief — one task per problem (searched 2026-10-30)

How to read this: I ran 14 searches and opened 5 papers (arXiv abstract pages).
Everything marked "abstract" comes from the abstract or search snippet only; I did
not read the full papers. Where sources are blog posts rather than papers I say so.
Nothing here has been tried in our harness. Several of our problems have no direct
2026 research; I say where.

## T1 Retrieval noise and context window (F5)
- **Standard recipe:** hybrid lexical + dense scoring over overlapping passages,
  with Maximal Marginal Relevance to cut redundant evidence
  ([TRUST Agents, arXiv 2604.12184](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.12184), abstract).
- **Sentence-level choice:** a 2025 shared-task study compared top-3 BM25 sentences
  with top-3 embedding sentences, and with whole documents, which kept context but
  added off-topic text ([ClaimIQ, arXiv 2509.11492](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.11492)).
- **Neighbouring-sentence window ("sentence window", "small-to-big"):** described
  in tutorials and glossaries only. I found no measured precision result for
  evidence verification; the sources themselves say to measure before adopting
  ([example](https://barkingiguana.com/writing/parent-document-retrieval-small-chunks-big-context/)).
- **For us:** stopwords + minimum overlap is within normal practice, and our offline
  replay on real queries is the right way to tune it. Adding dense scoring needs a
  local embedding model (a download; I would ask first). MMR targets our repeated
  identical sentences. The window must be measured on our own queries.

## T2 Documents arriving late: re-check only what is affected (F1, F4)
- **No 2026 work found** on streaming re-verification of earlier claims when new
  evidence arrives. Closest: iterative retrieve-and-verify loops (FIRE, 2024),
  persistent evidence memory reused across claims
  ([MERMAID, arXiv 2601.22361](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.22361)).
- **Belief revision:** [AGM-Bench (ICLR 2026)](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2026/10017503)
  reports LLMs show "belief inertia" (keeping retracted information) and
  "collateral damage" (retracting beliefs the new evidence did not touch)
  (snippet). A 2026 survey traces dependency-tracked updating back to truth
  maintenance systems ([arXiv 2608.14567](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.14567)).
- **For us:** this supports your design. Decide what a new document touches in
  deterministic code (retrieval per claim plus dependency tracking), not by asking
  a model which beliefs to drop. CFERP's dependency invalidation is already of this
  kind; it fails only because unprompted documents arrive with no known dependencies.

## T3 Settling and the budget (F2, F3)
- **Stopping on evidence coverage:** [HALT (arXiv 2608.02009, Findings of EMNLP
  2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02009) stops searching only when accumulated
  evidence supports every required claim, and stops without a confident answer when
  coverage cannot be verified. It reports less redundant search with exact match
  largely preserved; the abstract gives no figures.
- **Cost-aware stopping:** [CAM-DF, arXiv 2607.27083](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.27083)
  (tool acquisition, offline replays); semantic early stopping
  ([arXiv 2606.27009](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27009)).
- **Practice:** layered termination (hard budget, step cap, completion signal) —
  opinion posts, not studies
  ([example](https://tianpan.co/blog/2026-05-07-tool-call-convergence-agents-stopping-criteria)).
- **For us:** define "settled" as every claim either covered, or checked against
  every available document with nothing found; keep the budget only as a hard guard
  and count model calls. A result of "stopped, coverage unverified" is legitimate.

## T4 Judging: support, contradict, or not enough information (F6, F10)
- [Evidence Absence Is Not Evidence Insufficiency (arXiv 2605.26663, Findings of
  EMNLP 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26663): the ability to say "not enough
  information" does not transfer reliably between ways of constructing such cases;
  a good aggregate score can hide it. Report results by construction type.
- [Abstention-Aware Scientific Reasoning (arXiv 2602.14189)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14189):
  split a claim into minimal conditions, check each with NLI, abstain when evidence
  is insufficient. Abstention, not model choice, controlled error.
- A small NLI verifier showed not-enough-information recall of only about 44–47%
  ([model card](https://huggingface.co/DeliVali/AIDAM_VREAL_279M_V1.0.0); not a paper).
- [Local judges (arXiv 2609.13824)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13824): LLaMA-3-8B and
  Qwen2.5-7B were 97.3% and 92.3% self-consistent but correlated only 0.275 and 0.340
  with human ratings. Small study, general answer scoring, not stance labelling.
- **For us:** self-consistency is not accuracy, so we need a small human-labelled gold
  set (from your reference board). Splitting compound claims into conditions matches
  what our Specialist already does. The assessor needs a real abstain path and a rule
  that a missing record is not a contradiction or a resolution.

## T5 Requests and information gaps (F9–F11)
- Common design: detect the gap, judge whether it blocks progress, ask only the
  highest-value question, otherwise proceed on stated assumptions, cap questions
  ([InfoGatherer, arXiv 2603.05909](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.05909);
  [Ask or Assume?, arXiv 2603.26233](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2603.26233);
  [PROPER Agents, arXiv 2601.09926](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2601.09926);
  all abstract/snippet).
- **For us:** request dedupe, a "blocks progress" test and a cap are standard. The
  resolved-by-absence mistake is the T4 problem again. Our own override rules need to
  record which check fired.

## T6 Duplicate claims (F7)
- Memory systems use exact match, then semantic match above a threshold; or a
  three-way LLM decision (update / no-op / add) over candidates found by shared tags;
  conflicting items are marked invalid, not deleted
  ([AIM, arXiv 2609.12320](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12320);
  [Mem0, arXiv 2504.19413](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.19413);
  [PlugMem, arXiv 2603.03296](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03296)). A quoted 0.92
  similarity cutoff comes from a how-to page and is unverified.
- **For us:** normalised-text and entity match first, model only for borderline pairs;
  supersede, never delete (CFERP already has a superseded state).

## T7 Structured output and the ID slip (F13)
- Constrained decoding guarantees shape, not correct values; small models still err
  inside valid structure; retry only the failed part (blog posts, anecdotal)
  ([example](https://shop.zimaspace.com/blogs/tech-ai-hub/small-local-models-hallucinate-json-output)).
- **For us:** put the valid IDs in the schema as an `enum` per call, so the grammar
  rules out `mat_…` where `cl:…` belongs. No benchmark for small Ollama models found.

## T8 Simulated custodian and fair comparison (F12–F13)
- Fixed profile or frozen script makes agents comparable
  ([SimulBench](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.07641)). Naive "act as a user" prompting
  is verbose and unrealistic ([MirrorBench, arXiv 2601.08118](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.08118v1)).
  Simulators grounded in real behaviour are harsher: about 3 points lower task success
  than cooperative ones ([RealUserSim, arXiv 2605.20204](https://awesomepapers.io/papers/2605.20204)).
  Simulators reached ρ≈0.7 with human judgements on two tasks
  ([SimulatorArena](https://preview.aclanthology.org/setup/2025.emnlp-main.1786)).
- **For us:** the fact-sheet design with a pinned model fits. Include uncooperative
  replies (partial, irrelevant, "we don't have it"), since cooperative simulators
  overstate success. Simulator realism stays unvalidated against real custodians.

## T9 Measuring RCA quality (F14–F15, F8)
- [ORCA-bench (arXiv 2607.28545)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28545), latest version:
  1,079 oncall tasks; best accuracy 25.3% on medium and 10.0% on hard; weakest model
  proposed an implausible root cause in 40% of reports. The search snippet gave 884
  tasks and 48.8%, so versions differ; trust neither without reading the paper. It is
  software oncall, not physical incidents.
- Failure taxonomies: 12 pitfall types on OpenRCA ([Kim 2026](https://cloudintelligenceworkshop.org/papers/aiops26-Kim.pdf));
  16 multi-hop reasoning failures (Riddell, FORGE '26).
- Event and causal factor trees record what evidence says occurred; fault trees
  explore possible causes; AI is described as automating evidence gathering, not
  judgement (blog posts: [one](https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-07-31-five-whys-vs-causal-tree/markdown)).
- **For us:** score against your reference board and label our run failures with a
  taxonomy. Keep the board from declaring a root cause, as it does now.

## T10 Symbolic search (SAHS)
- LLMs writing ASP with self-correction loops
  ([arXiv 2604.27960](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.27960)). No 2026 study of our
  combination found. Low priority.

## Gaps in this search
No direct 2026 research found on: streaming re-verification (T2), measured gains for
neighbour-sentence windows (T1), or building cause-and-effect charts from incident
documents in industrial settings (T9). That means "not found in 14 searches", not
"does not exist".

- **Stopping on evidence coverage:** [HALT (arXiv 2608.02009, Findings of EMNLP
  2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02009) stops searching only when accumulated
  evidence supports every required claim, and stops without a confident answer when
  coverage cannot be verified. It reports less redundant search with exact match
  largely preserved; the abstract gives no figures.
- **Cost-aware stopping:** [CAM-DF, arXiv 2607.27083](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.27083)
  (tool acquisition, offline replays); semantic early stopping
  ([arXiv 2606.27009](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27009)).
- **Practice:** layered termination (hard budget, step cap, completion signal) —
  opinion posts, not studies
  ([example](https://tianpan.co/blog/2026-05-07-tool-call-convergence-agents-stopping-criteria)).
- **For us:** define "settled" as every claim either covered, or checked against
  every available document with nothing found; keep the budget only as a hard guard
  and count model calls. A result of "stopped, coverage unverified" is legitimate.

## T4 Judging: support, contradict, or not enough information (F6, F10)
- [Evidence Absence Is Not Evidence Insufficiency (arXiv 2605.26663, Findings of
  EMNLP 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26663): the ability to say "not enough
  information" does not transfer reliably between ways of constructing such cases;
  a good aggregate score can hide it. Report results by construction type.
- [Abstention-Aware Scientific Reasoning (arXiv 2602.14189)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14189):
  split a claim into minimal conditions, check each with NLI, abstain when evidence
  is insufficient. Abstention, not model choice, controlled error.
- A small NLI verifier showed not-enough-information recall of only about 44–47%
  ([model card](https://huggingface.co/DeliVali/AIDAM_VREAL_279M_V1.0.0); not a paper).
- [Local judges (arXiv 2609.13824)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13824): LLaMA-3-8B and
  Qwen2.5-7B were 97.3% and 92.3% self-consistent but correlated only 0.275 and 0.340
  with human ratings. Small study, general answer scoring, not stance labelling.
- **For us:** self-consistency is not accuracy, so we need a small human-labelled gold
  set (from your reference board). Splitting compound claims into conditions matches
  what our Specialist already does. The assessor needs a real abstain path and a rule
  that a missing record is not a contradiction or a resolution.

## T5 Requests and information gaps (F9–F11)
- Common design: detect the gap, judge whether it blocks progress, ask only the
  highest-value question, otherwise proceed on stated assumptions, cap questions
  ([InfoGatherer, arXiv 2603.05909](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.05909);
  [Ask or Assume?, arXiv 2603.26233](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2603.26233);
  [PROPER Agents, arXiv 2601.09926](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2601.09926);
  all abstract/snippet).
- **For us:** request dedupe, a "blocks progress" test and a cap are standard. The
  resolved-by-absence mistake is the T4 problem again. Our own override rules need to
  record which check fired.

## T6 Duplicate claims (F7)
- Memory systems use exact match, then semantic match above a threshold; or a
  three-way LLM decision (update / no-op / add) over candidates found by shared tags;
  conflicting items are marked invalid, not deleted
  ([AIM, arXiv 2609.12320](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12320);
  [Mem0, arXiv 2504.19413](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.19413);
  [PlugMem, arXiv 2603.03296](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03296)). A quoted 0.92
  similarity cutoff comes from a how-to page and is unverified.
- **For us:** normalised-text and entity match first, model only for borderline pairs;
  supersede, never delete (CFERP already has a superseded state).

## T7 Structured output and the ID slip (F13)
- Constrained decoding guarantees shape, not correct values; small models still err
  inside valid structure; retry only the failed part (blog posts, anecdotal)
  ([example](https://shop.zimaspace.com/blogs/tech-ai-hub/small-local-models-hallucinate-json-output)).
- **For us:** put the valid IDs in the schema as an `enum` per call, so the grammar
  rules out `mat_…` where `cl:…` belongs. No benchmark for small Ollama models found.

## T8 Simulated custodian and fair comparison (F12–F13)
- Fixed profile or frozen script makes agents comparable
  ([SimulBench](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.07641)). Naive "act as a user" prompting
  is verbose and unrealistic ([MirrorBench, arXiv 2601.08118](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.08118v1)).
  Simulators grounded in real behaviour are harsher: about 3 points lower task success
  than cooperative ones ([RealUserSim, arXiv 2605.20204](https://awesomepapers.io/papers/2605.20204)).
  Simulators reached ρ≈0.7 with human judgements on two tasks
  ([SimulatorArena](https://preview.aclanthology.org/setup/2025.emnlp-main.1786)).
- **For us:** the fact-sheet design with a pinned model fits. Include uncooperative
  replies (partial, irrelevant, "we don't have it"), since cooperative simulators
  overstate success. Simulator realism stays unvalidated against real custodians.

## T9 Measuring RCA quality (F14–F15, F8)
- [ORCA-bench (arXiv 2607.28545)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28545), latest version:
  1,079 oncall tasks; best accuracy 25.3% on medium and 10.0% on hard; weakest model
  proposed an implausible root cause in 40% of reports. The search snippet gave 884
  tasks and 48.8%, so versions differ; trust neither without reading the paper. It is
  software oncall, not physical incidents.
- Failure taxonomies: 12 pitfall types on OpenRCA ([Kim 2026](https://cloudintelligenceworkshop.org/papers/aiops26-Kim.pdf));
  16 multi-hop reasoning failures (Riddell, FORGE '26).
- Event and causal factor trees record what evidence says occurred; fault trees
  explore possible causes; AI is described as automating evidence gathering, not
  judgement (blog posts: [one](https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-07-31-five-whys-vs-causal-tree/markdown)).
- **For us:** score against your reference board and label our run failures with a
  taxonomy. Keep the board from declaring a root cause, as it does now.

## T10 Symbolic search (SAHS)
- LLMs writing ASP with self-correction loops
  ([arXiv 2604.27960](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.27960)). No 2026 study of our
  combination found. Low priority.

## Gaps in this search
No direct 2026 research found on: streaming re-verification (T2), measured gains for
neighbour-sentence windows (T1), or building cause-and-effect charts from incident
documents in industrial settings (T9). That means "not found in 14 searches", not
"does not exist".

# Closed-loop V3 scenario runbook

This file is the operator guide for running and troubleshooting the V3 synthetic
R3 workflow. The implementation is in `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/`; this guide
describes the control path and where to inspect behavior.

## What this run does

1. PIRIS receives the opening case packet and opening documents.
2. CFERP Lead builds/updates the investigation board and queues work.
3. The V3 bridge runs Specialist, Evidence Worker, and Assessor jobs within the
   configured job limit. Role calls use the configured model client.
4. Only requests that reached Assessor approval are dispatched by the runner.
5. The synthetic custodian sees only the current later-material wave. Its model
   call may select fixture document IDs and slot IDs; Python rejects unknown,
   duplicate, or extra values.
6. Selected documents are submitted as request-linked material through PIRIS.
   Other documents in the wave enter as unrequested uploads.
7. The role queue runs again. Later material can invalidate dependent work and
   trigger reassessment through the ordinary CFERP lifecycle.
8. After the fixture waves, unanswered requests get one bounded search across
   the fixture corpus per loop round. A no-match note explicitly says it is not
   proof that the requested record does not exist.
9. A hard round limit stops an unbounded sequence of newly generated requests.

The simulation does **not** decide the incident cause, mark a case closed, or
send messages to a real person. Human response and actual external dispatch
remain operator responsibilities in a real investigation.

## Files to know

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py` | Scenario driver, dispatch/reply loop, output snapshot |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/orchestration/fixture_outward_responder.py` | Constrained model call and Python validation of selected IDs |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/orchestration/v3_runtime.py` | PIRIS-to-CFERP material registration and role queue boundary |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/cferp/` | Lead, queue, board, request lifecycle, versioning, and invalidation |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/sahs/` | Specialist candidate generation/search |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/ewv3/` | Evidence search and packet production |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/hera1/` | Assessor review |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/piris/` | Intake registration, extraction, indexing, and request linkage |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/tests/` | Role, lifecycle, integration, and closed-loop responder tests |
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/examples/r3_synthetic_case.json` | Self-contained scenario definition relative to this archive |

## Run

From the combined archive root, install the V3 requirements and ensure Ollama
is running with a model already installed:

```bash
python -m pip install -r V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/requirements-sahs.txt
ollama list
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py \
  --provider ollama_native \
  --model <exact-tag-from-ollama-list> \
  --base-url http://localhost:11434 \
  --max-jobs 64 \
  --max-rounds 12 \
  --output outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

OpenRouter can be used instead by setting `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the shell and
omitting `--provider ollama_native`:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py \
  --model <OpenRouter-model-id> \
  --output outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

If using the separate `R3_Synthetic_Example_Bundle.zip`, extract it and pass its
`r3_synthetic_case.json` path with `--case`. Its material paths are relative to
that JSON and remain inside the extracted bundle.

## Read the output

The JSON contains:

- `board`: current claims, causal links, branches, assessments, requests,
  needs, and registered materials;
- `work` and `assignments`: role queue state, including unfinished work;
- `lead_events`: ordered state changes from the Lead workflow;
- `intake_submissions`: each opening, response, and unrequested upload handled
  by PIRIS;
- `model_calls`: provider call records, including the synthetic custodian task;
- `closed_loop_simulation.outward_trace`: request dispatch, response source IDs,
  slot IDs, unrequested material arrivals, and round-limit events;
- `run_metadata`: provider/model label, job budget, completion status, and any
  caught failure.

`run_status: completed` means the runner reached its bounded end without an
exception. It does not mean every request was answered or the case is ready to
close. Inspect `board.requests`, `board.needs`, `work`, and the final case state.

### Run status, job failures, and exit codes

| `run_status` | Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | 0 | Reached its bounded end; no role result was rejected. |
| `completed_with_job_failures` | 2 | Reached its bounded end, but at least one job was rejected and recorded (below). |
| `failed_or_partial` | 1 | Aborted by an exception; `run_metadata.failure` says which. |

When a role's own engine reports that it rejected its output (SAHS, EWV3 or HERA
returned a failure status), the job ends `FAILED`, nothing from it is committed,
and the run continues. Each one is listed in `run_metadata.job_failures` (and at
the top level as `job_failures`) with the role, status, targets, and the engine's
reason, and the event log has an `assignment_failed` entry. The claim or passage
that job covered **stays unassessed**; a failed job is never evidence. The runner
stops with `failed_or_partial` once `--max-job-failures` (default 25; 0 aborts on
the first) is exceeded.

These still abort the run, because they point at the harness rather than one bad
reply: commit-gate errors from CFERP (for example unknown rule IDs), adapter
`IntegrationError`s, HERA/CFERP disagreeing about staleness, and code errors.

`completed_role_jobs` and `role_jobs_remaining` come from the bridge's own
counter, so they are correct even when a run aborts mid-queue. Outputs written
before this change show `[]` and a full remaining budget on aborted runs; do not
rely on those two fields in old files.

### Scoring runs

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_run.py outputs/run_a.json outputs/run_b.json
```

It prints reliability (status, what aborted it, job failures), efficiency (jobs
executed, model calls, extraction calls per assessor job, repeat work), evidence
signals (assessment mix, share with nothing extracted, distinct claim-and-sentence
pairs), and how far the loop got (requests dispatched and answered, waves arrived),
plus a completion tally across files. Use `--json` for machine-readable numbers.
These are workflow signals on synthetic fixtures. "Nothing extracted" is a proxy
for retrieval noise, not a measure of truth, and `neutral` can be correct.

### Fixed custodian (default)

`run_v3_closed_loop.py` now defaults to `--custodian fixed`. The simulated custodian is
deterministic and never uses the model under test, so two models can be compared on
the same simulated world. It lives in `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/orchestration/custodian.py`
and is configured by `ground_truth/custodian_holdings.json` (documents it holds, when each
-----
# What each problem must achieve for the full framework

Written 2026-10-30 from the audit (`FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md`), your description of how
the system should behave, and a second round of research. Nothing here is
implemented. Numeric targets are proposals: I will fix them only after we have a
baseline from the scorecard on the fixed simulator.

## The overall goal

Given an incident and documents that arrive at any time (with the incident, in
answer to the system's own requests, or unprompted), the framework keeps
investigating with whatever it has and maintains an RCA board such that:

- **G1 Grounded.** Every statement on the board traces to a source sentence.
- **G2 Honest.** The board separates what the evidence shows from what is only
  proposed or unresolved, and never declares a root cause the evidence does not
  support. A missing record is never treated as a finding.
- **G3 Responsive.** A document arriving at any moment is checked against every
  existing claim; only what it touches is redone.
- **G4 Asks well.** It requests the evidence that would change the board, once,
  and does not wait idle for the reply.
- **G5 Order-independent.** The same documents in a different order or at different
  times give the same board, up to model noise.
- **G6 Comparable.** Two local models can be compared on a fixed simulation, scored
  against the reference board.

The reference board's own statuses are the target vocabulary: observed event,
reported interpretation, proposed mechanism, unresolved premise; support status
supported / proposed / unresolved; combination AND / OR / unspecified. Our board
today has claim kinds and an incident status, not these. That mapping is part of T10.

## Task list

Each task: what it must achieve, how we would know, what the research offers, what
is uncertain.

### T1 Retrieval: find the right sentences (G1, G3)
- **Must achieve:** for each claim, the sentences that bear on it are in the
  candidate set, and few others are.
- **Acceptance (proposed):** recall of 100% on the key sentences the reference board
  needs (starting with the 3 valve sentences and the sealing-test sentence); share of
  assessments with nothing extracted falls well below the current 82%; measured on
  real queries from saved runs before any live run.
- **Research:** hybrid BM25 plus dense with MMR to cut redundancy
  ([TRUST Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.12184)). [MERMAID](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.22361)
  keys evidence by entity, recalls BM25 top-3 chunks then re-ranks sentences
  semantically (top 20), de-duplicates, applies a diversity filter and a token cap;
  hybrid recall beat BM25-only (Macro-F1 0.76 to 0.80 on BingCheck). Local
  cross-encoder rerankers exist for Ollama
  ([guide](https://www.codewords.ai/blog/ollama-reranker)); vendor claims of
  double-digit gains, no claim-verification test found.
- **Plan implied:** stopwords plus a 2-shared-term floor (cheap, offline-testable),
  entity-keyed lookup (valve ID, component names, times), then an optional reranker
  only if the gold set shows the lexical stage still leaves noise. Neighbour window:
  untested in the literature, so we decide on our own data.
- **Uncertain:** a reranker or embedding model is a download; neighbour-window
  benefit is unmeasured anywhere I looked.

### T2 Absorb a new document (G3, G5)

Each task: what it must achieve, how we would know, what the research offers, what
is uncertain.

### T1 Retrieval: find the right sentences (G1, G3)
- **Must achieve:** for each claim, the sentences that bear on it are in the
  candidate set, and few others are.
- **Acceptance (proposed):** recall of 100% on the key sentences the reference board
  needs (starting with the 3 valve sentences and the sealing-test sentence); share of
  assessments with nothing extracted falls well below the current 82%; measured on
  real queries from saved runs before any live run.
- **Research:** hybrid BM25 plus dense with MMR to cut redundancy
  ([TRUST Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.12184)). [MERMAID](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.22361)
  keys evidence by entity, recalls BM25 top-3 chunks then re-ranks sentences
  semantically (top 20), de-duplicates, applies a diversity filter and a token cap;
  hybrid recall beat BM25-only (Macro-F1 0.76 to 0.80 on BingCheck). Local
  cross-encoder rerankers exist for Ollama
  ([guide](https://www.codewords.ai/blog/ollama-reranker)); vendor claims of
  double-digit gains, no claim-verification test found.
- **Plan implied:** stopwords plus a 2-shared-term floor (cheap, offline-testable),
  entity-keyed lookup (valve ID, component names, times), then an optional reranker
  only if the gold set shows the lexical stage still leaves noise. Neighbour window:
  untested in the literature, so we decide on our own data.
- **Uncertain:** a reranker or embedding model is a download; neighbour-window
  benefit is unmeasured anywhere I looked.

### T2 Absorb a new document (G3, G5)
- **Must achieve:** a new document, however it arrives, is checked against every

Score a closed-loop run output against the human RCA chart and gold evidence map.

Inputs are the two confirmed files in ``ground_truth/``: the chart transcription
(nodes, links, open items) and the evidence map (which sentences in E01-E16 bear on
each node, plus designed traps). The run output is the JSON written by
``run_v3_closed_loop.py``.

What it reports, and what it does not claim:
- **node coverage** compares each chart node with the run's claims by word overlap.
  That is a crude match, so every match is listed with its score for you to audit;
  a node can be matched wrongly or missed. Tune ``--threshold`` and look at the list.
- **key sentences** says whether the sentences the evidence map marks as important
  were ever assessed, and whether the stance the run gave them is sensible
  (a sentence the map marks "insufficient" must not be called supporting or
  contradicting).
- **traps** checks the packet's designed mistakes (see the evidence map).

content.text:
I've paused the README rewrite and haven't written anything yet. While gathering facts for it, I found something you should decide on first.

`ground_truth/r3_human_rca_chart.json` is now in your **public** repo. It's a transcription of what looks like a real company RCA report, not a synthetic fixture:
- **Source:** "Root Cause Analysis Report 16515, rev 0, 10/14/2024, CauseLink", titled "[PLANT-ABBR] SIFp-80HSM: R3 Carrier Beam Near Miss 10.14.24".
- **Person:** the team field names one person.
- **Details:** the business unit "80 HSM - Roughing Mill", a $50,000 damage figure, timings, all 23 cause nodes and the proposed solutions.

The case documents E01–E16 say they are synthetic, but this chart doesn't. If it's real and not yours to publish, there are two levels of fix:
- **Make the repo private:** quick and easy to undo, and it stops public access right away.
- **Remove the file completely:** deleting it in a new commit isn't enough, because it stays in the history. That needs a history rewrite and a force-push to `main`, which I'd only do with your explicit go-ahead.

Either way, it was public for about a day, so someone could already have copied it. If the data is fine to share, I'll carry on with the README.

operator action.

|---|---|
| Lead | `cferp/` |
| Specialist | `sahs/` |
| Evidence Worker | `ewv3/` |
| Assessor | `hera1/` |

unrequested uploads; the Lead and role pipeline then process the arrivals.

the output JSON. It does not auto-send outward questions.

The runner uses one OpenRouter model for PIRIS metadata suggestions, the
optional CFERP semantic helper, SAHS, EWV3, and HERA1. CFERP's hard rules,

input.content:
# Root Cause Analysis with cooperating LLM roles

A research harness for building an incident root cause analysis (RCA) from documents,
using five cooperating roles driven by a local or hosted language model. It is tested
on one synthetic industrial incident and scored against a human-made RCA chart for
that incident.

The question it studies: can a model, split into bounded roles with Python checks
between them, keep investigating as documents arrive at any time, check each document
against every claim, ask for missing evidence, and build an RCA board without
declaring a root cause the evidence does not support?

This is research code (v0.4). It is not a product, and the results below come from
single runs on one case.

## The test case

**R3 carrier beam fall.** A raised delivery carrier beam on a rolling-mill roughing
stand fell into the mill pit and struck an equipment sled and a temporary scaffold.
Nobody was hurt. The case has 16 documents (E01–E16): the incident notice, functional
descriptions, inspection notes, test results, logs and statements. All of them are
synthetic research fixtures, not real company records.

Documents arrive in waves: some with the incident, some only when the system asks for
them, and some unprompted.

## How it works

| Role | Package | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | `piris/` | Registers each arriving document, extracts and indexes its text, and links replies to the request that asked for them. It does not judge evidence. |
| Lead | `cferp/` | Keeps the investigation board (claims, causal links, requests, open needs), queues work for the other roles, and redoes only the work a new document affects. |
| Specialist | `sahs/` | Proposes candidate causes and mechanisms as typed propositions and rules. Python validates them, and Clingo (answer set programming) composes candidate explanations. |
| Evidence Worker | `ewv3/` | Finds the sentences in the documents that bear on a claim and builds an evidence packet. |
| Assessor | `hera1/` | Judges each packet: supports, contradicts, or not enough information. It also approves outward requests for missing evidence. |

One closed-loop run goes like this:

1. Intake receives the incident notice and the first documents. The Lead builds the board.
2. The Specialist, Evidence Worker and Assessor jobs run, up to a job limit.
3. Requests the Assessor approved go to a **simulated custodian**, which releases the
   documents it holds. By default it is deterministic and never uses the model under
   test (`ground_truth/custodian_holdings.json`), so two models face the same world.
4. Released documents re-enter through Intake. The loop repeats until the waves run
   out or a round limit is reached.

The model proposes and judges. Python decides what a claim's status is, rejects
references to IDs that don't exist, and never lets the run mark a root cause on its
own. A missing record is treated as a gap, not as a finding.

## Ground truth and scoring

`ground_truth/` holds what runs are scored against:

- `r3_human_rca_chart.json`: a transcription of the human RCA chart for the case
  (23 cause nodes, 14 cause links, open questions and proposed solutions).
- `evidence_map_draft.json`: which sentences in E01–E16 bear on each chart node, plus
  designed traps such as passages that look relevant but settle nothing.
- `custodian_holdings.json`: which documents the simulated custodian holds and when it
  releases them.

`V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py` reports how many chart
nodes the board covers, whether the key sentences were assessed with a sensible
stance, and whether the traps were avoided. Node matching is by word overlap, so it
lists every match for you to check.

## Results so far

gpt-oss:20b on Ollama, 256 role jobs per run, fixed custodian, one run each. The
**context** column is the Ollama context window; "6k kept free" means 6,000 tokens
of it were reserved for the Specialist's reasoning and answer, with its prompt
trimmed to fit the rest.

| | Earlier fix | 16k, 6k kept free | 32k | 32k, low effort | 32k, medium effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key supporting sentences found | 3/14 | 5/14 | 5/14 | 2/14 | 3/14 |
| Key sentences assessed | 17 | 17 | 19 | 17 | 20 |
| Documents used | 14 | 14 | 16 | 14 | 15 |
| Overclaimed sentences | 5 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| Claims on the board | 24 | 35 | 40 | 30 | 40 |
| Failed jobs | 14 | 4 | 13 | 3 | 14 |
| Cut-off answers | 41 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Run time | – | ~3¾ h | ~5⅓ h | ~1¾ h | ~4 h |

What this shows so far:

- Keeping room for the answer removed cut-off answers.
- A larger window let more documents reach the Specialist and cut overclaiming.
- Lower reasoning effort was faster but found less. High effort was too slow to finish
  (about 15 jobs an hour).
- **The board still rarely reaches the causes on the chart.** The Specialist only
  looks at documents through the claims already on the board, so evidence that fits
  no current claim never steers it. Directing it at one document at a time is being
  tested as the next step.

Caveats: each column is a single run, so differences of one or two may be noise.
The "supporting sentences" count is generous, because it credits a support on any
claim. Run outputs (50–110 MB each) are not in this repository.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` | The current five-role system, its runners, scorers and tests. [Its README](V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/README.md) covers each role in detail. |
| `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/` | Earlier versions kept for comparison: V1 is prompt-only, V2 adds research-inspired methods and rules. They share one codebase and are selected by profile (see its `VERSION_GUIDE.md`). The R3 documents live in its test fixtures. |
| `ground_truth/` | The human RCA chart, the evidence map and the custodian holdings. |
| `scripts/` | Launchers that run V1, V2 and V3 on the same case. |
| `tests_ollama/` | Tests for the Ollama client. |

## Setup

Tested with Python 3.13. Clingo is the only V3 dependency:

```bash
python -m pip install -r V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/requirements-sahs.txt
```

For local models, install [Ollama](https://ollama.com) and pull a model first, for
example `ollama pull gpt-oss:20b`. For hosted models, set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in your
shell. See `.env.example` in the V1/V2 codebase; never commit a real key.

## Run

All commands run from the repository root.

One closed-loop run on a local model:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py \
  --provider ollama_native --model gpt-oss:20b \
  --num-ctx 32768 --answer-reserve 6000 \
  --max-jobs 256 --call-timeout 600 \
  --output outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

Several runs of one configuration, with the spread between them:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_repeats.py \
  --provider ollama_native --model gpt-oss:20b --runs 3 \
  --num-ctx 32768 --answer-reserve 6000 \
  --output-prefix outputs/gptoss_32k
```

Score a run against the ground truth, and check its workflow health:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_run.py outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

Run the tests, which use scripted model replies and need no model:

```bash
cd V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired
PYTHONPATH=. python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

`--help` on any script lists every option. To run V1, V2 and V3 on the same case,
use `scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py` (see [OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md](OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md)).

## Further reading

- [CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md](CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md): how a run works, its output, exit codes and failures.
- [FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md](FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md): the goals (grounded, honest, responsive, asks well, order-independent, comparable) and the tasks toward them.
- [FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md](FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md): the problems found in earlier runs.
- [RESEARCH_BRIEF.md](RESEARCH_BRIEF.md): related research for each problem.
- [OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md](OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md): the native Ollama client.
- `CHANGELOG_v0.2.md` to `CHANGELOG_v0.4.md`: version history.

A research harness for building an incident root cause analysis (RCA) from documents,
using five cooperating roles driven by a local or hosted language model. It is tested
on one synthetic industrial incident and scored against a human-made RCA chart for
that incident.

The question it studies: can a model, split into bounded roles with Python checks
between them, keep investigating as documents arrive at any time, check each document
against every claim, ask for missing evidence, and build an RCA board without
declaring a root cause the evidence does not support?

This is research code (v0.4). It is not a product, and the results below come from
single runs on one case.

## The test case

**R3 carrier beam fall.** A raised delivery carrier beam on a rolling-mill roughing
stand fell into the mill pit and struck an equipment sled and a temporary scaffold.
Nobody was hurt. The case has 16 documents (E01–E16): the incident notice, functional
descriptions, inspection notes, test results, logs and statements. All of them are
synthetic research fixtures, not real company records.

Documents arrive in waves: some with the incident, some only when the system asks for
them, and some unprompted.

## How it works

| Role | Package | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | `piris/` | Registers each arriving document, extracts and indexes its text, and links replies to the request that asked for them. It does not judge evidence. |
| Lead | `cferp/` | Keeps the investigation board (claims, causal links, requests, open needs), queues work for the other roles, and redoes only the work a new document affects. |
| Specialist | `sahs/` | Proposes candidate causes and mechanisms as typed propositions and rules. Python validates them, and Clingo (answer set programming) composes candidate explanations. |
| Evidence Worker | `ewv3/` | Finds the sentences in the documents that bear on a claim and builds an evidence packet. |
| Assessor | `hera1/` | Judges each packet: supports, contradicts, or not enough information. It also approves outward requests for missing evidence. |

One closed-loop run goes like this:

1. Intake receives the incident notice and the first documents. The Lead builds the board.
2. The Specialist, Evidence Worker and Assessor jobs run, up to a job limit.
3. Requests the Assessor approved go to a **simulated custodian**, which releases the
   documents it holds. By default it is deterministic and never uses the model under
   test (`ground_truth/custodian_holdings.json`), so two models face the same world.
4. Released documents re-enter through Intake. The loop repeats until the waves run
   out or a round limit is reached.

The model proposes and judges. Python decides what a claim's status is, rejects
references to IDs that don't exist, and never lets the run mark a root cause on its
own. A missing record is treated as a gap, not as a finding.

## Ground truth and scoring

`ground_truth/` holds what runs are scored against:

- `r3_human_rca_chart.json`: a transcription of the human RCA chart for the case
  (23 cause nodes, 14 cause links, open questions and proposed solutions).
- `evidence_map_draft.json`: which sentences in E01–E16 bear on each chart node, plus
  designed traps such as passages that look relevant but settle nothing.
- `custodian_holdings.json`: which documents the simulated custodian holds and when it
  releases them.

`V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py` reports how many chart
nodes the board covers, whether the key sentences were assessed with a sensible
stance, and whether the traps were avoided. Node matching is by word overlap, so it
lists every match for you to check.

## Results so far

gpt-oss:20b on Ollama, 256 role jobs per run, fixed custodian, one run each. The
**context** column is the Ollama context window; "6k kept free" means 6,000 tokens
of it were reserved for the Specialist's reasoning and answer, with its prompt
trimmed to fit the rest.

| | Earlier fix | 16k, 6k kept free | 32k | 32k, low effort | 32k, medium effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key supporting sentences found | 3/14 | 5/14 | 5/14 | 2/14 | 3/14 |
| Key sentences assessed | 17 | 17 | 19 | 17 | 20 |
| Documents used | 14 | 14 | 16 | 14 | 15 |
| Overclaimed sentences | 5 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| Claims on the board | 24 | 35 | 40 | 30 | 40 |
| Failed jobs | 14 | 4 | 13 | 3 | 14 |
| Cut-off answers | 41 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Run time | – | ~3¾ h | ~5⅓ h | ~1¾ h | ~4 h |

What this shows so far:

- Keeping room for the answer removed cut-off answers.
- A larger window let more documents reach the Specialist and cut overclaiming.
- Lower reasoning effort was faster but found less. High effort was too slow to finish
  (about 15 jobs an hour).
- **The board still rarely reaches the causes on the chart.** The Specialist only
  looks at documents through the claims already on the board, so evidence that fits
  no current claim never steers it. Directing it at one document at a time is being
  tested as the next step.

Caveats: each column is a single run, so differences of one or two may be noise.
The "supporting sentences" count is generous, because it credits a support on any
claim. Run outputs (50–110 MB each) are not in this repository.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` | The current five-role system, its runners, scorers and tests. [Its README](V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/README.md) covers each role in detail. |
| `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/` | Earlier versions kept for comparison: V1 is prompt-only, V2 adds research-inspired methods and rules. They share one codebase and are selected by profile (see its `VERSION_GUIDE.md`). The R3 documents live in its test fixtures. |
| `ground_truth/` | The human RCA chart, the evidence map and the custodian holdings. |
| `scripts/` | Launchers that run V1, V2 and V3 on the same case. |
| `tests_ollama/` | Tests for the Ollama client. |

## Setup

Tested with Python 3.13. Clingo is the only V3 dependency:

```bash
python -m pip install -r V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/requirements-sahs.txt
```

For local models, install [Ollama](https://ollama.com) and pull a model first, for
example `ollama pull gpt-oss:20b`. For hosted models, set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in your
shell. See `.env.example` in the V1/V2 codebase; never commit a real key.

## Run

All commands run from the repository root.

One closed-loop run on a local model:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py \
  --provider ollama_native --model gpt-oss:20b \
  --num-ctx 32768 --answer-reserve 6000 \
  --max-jobs 256 --call-timeout 600 \
  --output outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

Several runs of one configuration, with the spread between them:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_repeats.py \
  --provider ollama_native --model gpt-oss:20b --runs 3 \
  --num-ctx 32768 --answer-reserve 6000 \
  --output-prefix outputs/gptoss_32k
```

Score a run against the ground truth, and check its workflow health:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_run.py outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

Run the tests, which use scripted model replies and need no model:

```bash
cd V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired
PYTHONPATH=. python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

`--help` on any script lists every option. To run V1, V2 and V3 on the same case,
use `scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py` (see [OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md](OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md)).

## Further reading

- [CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md](CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md): how a run works, its output, exit codes and failures.
- [FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md](FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md): the goals (grounded, honest, responsive, asks well, order-independent, comparable) and the tasks toward them.
- [FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md](FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md): the problems found in earlier runs.
- [RESEARCH_BRIEF.md](RESEARCH_BRIEF.md): related research for each problem.
- [OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md](OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md): the native Ollama client.
- `CHANGELOG_v0.2.md` to `CHANGELOG_v0.4.md`: version history.

# RCA implementation versions: V1, V2, and V3 (combined v0.3)

This archive preserves the earlier prompt/rule implementations and packages the current V3 role implementations together for review.

This update corrects the multi-claim Evidence Worker handoff to HERA and adds a native local Ollama adapter for all three versions. See `CHANGELOG_v0.3.md` and `OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md`.

The V3 package now also includes `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py`, a closed-loop synthetic scenario runner that dispatches Assessor-approved outward requests, simulates a constrained fixture custodian response, re-ingests replies through PIRIS, and resumes V3 role processing. See the V3 README for scope and commands.

| Version | Label | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Prompt-only baseline | The original five-role baseline in the legacy codebase; select `config/experiments/v1_basic.yaml`. |
| V2 | Prompts plus methods/rules | The original research-inspired role methods and prompts; select `config/experiments/v2_full.yaml`. |
| V3 | Neurosymbolic-inspired prototype | Standalone CFERP Lead, SAHS Specialist, EWV3 Evidence Worker, HERA1 Assessor, PIRIS Intake, and an Intake-to-Lead runtime. |

## Layout

- `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/Original_V1_V2_Codebase.zip` is the supplied V1/V2 archive unchanged.
- `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/source/` is its extracted copy. The included `VERSION_GUIDE.md` maps the exact implementations and profiles. The copy includes a runner-only `case_id` option so the bundled R3 fixture keeps its own case identity; the V1/V2 role implementations are unchanged.
- `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` contains the current role package source and selected tests. SAHS uses LLM proposal generation, typed causal representations, Python validation, and ASP/Clingo candidate composition. The other roles provide retrieval, assessment, coordination, and provenance functions; not every role independently uses a symbolic solver.
- `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/orchestration/v3_bridge.py` routes queued CFERP work to SAHS, EWV3, and HERA1. `v3_runtime.py` runs PIRIS for initial and later submissions, converts registered materials to CFERP records, and starts or refreshes Lead work. The host/operator still controls external request dispatch and human responses.

## Testing

Run tests from `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` after installing `requirements-sahs.txt` (Clingo is required for SAHS):

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements-sahs.txt
PYTHONPATH=. python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

The V3 label describes the architecture and implementation direction. It does not claim that every role independently uses a symbolic solver. Package and integration tests use scripted model responses; no OpenRouter live call is included in this archive.

## Live V1/V2/V3 run

The combined launcher runs the V1 prompt-only profile, V2 full profile, and V3 pipeline sequentially on the bundled staged R3 fixture. Run it from this directory:

```bash
python -m pip install -r V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/requirements-sahs.txt
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="your-key-in-your-shell"
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py --check-only
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py \
  --case V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/examples/r3_synthetic_case.json \
  --model nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free \
  --output outputs/r3_all_versions
```

The case materials are synthetic research fixtures, not authentic company records. The launcher saves separate V1/V2 and V3 outputs plus a combined status report. It is an exploratory workflow comparison, not a controlled causal-quality comparison: V1/V2 use a custodian/request loop, while V3 receives staged PIRIS material arrivals. The full V3 instructions are in `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/README.md`.

## Run against a local Ollama model

The archive includes a native Ollama `/api/chat` adapter. It uses only the Python standard library, sends JSON-mode requests, records local token/timing metadata, and never switches to fixture responses. Install and start Ollama separately, then pull a model supported by your machine:

```bash
ollama pull <model-tag>
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py \
  --provider ollama_native \
  --model <model-tag> \
  --base-url http://localhost:11434 \
  --check-only
python scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py \
  --provider ollama_native \
  --model <model-tag> \
  --base-url http://localhost:11434 \
  --output outputs/r3_ollama
```

Use the exact tag shown by `ollama list`; the preflight checks `/api/tags` before starting either pipeline. This runs V1, V2, and V3 through the native local API. No OpenRouter or OpenAI key is needed. See `OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md` for direct Python use, configuration, tests, and the distinction between native Ollama and the existing OpenAI-compatible Ollama endpoint.

# Root Cause Analysis with cooperating LLM roles

A research harness for building an incident root cause analysis (RCA) from documents,
using five cooperating roles driven by a local or hosted language model. It is tested
on one synthetic industrial incident and scored against a human-made RCA chart for
that incident.

The question it studies: can a model, split into bounded roles with Python checks
between them, keep investigating as documents arrive at any time, check each document
against every claim, ask for missing evidence, and build an RCA board without
declaring a root cause the evidence does not support?

This is research code (v0.4). It is not a product, and the results below come from
single runs on one case.

## The test case

**R3 carrier beam fall.** A raised delivery carrier beam on a rolling-mill roughing
stand fell into the mill pit and struck an equipment sled and a temporary scaffold.
Nobody was hurt. The case has 16 documents (E01–E16): the incident notice, functional
descriptions, inspection notes, test results, logs and statements. All of them are
synthetic research fixtures, not real company records.

Documents arrive in waves: some with the incident, some only when the system asks for
them, and some unprompted.

## How it works

| Role | Package | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | `piris/` | Registers each arriving document, extracts and indexes its text, and links replies to the request that asked for them. It does not judge evidence. |
| Lead | `cferp/` | Keeps the investigation board (claims, causal links, requests, open needs), queues work for the other roles, and redoes only the work a new document affects. |
| Specialist | `sahs/` | Proposes candidate causes and mechanisms as typed propositions and rules. Python validates them, and Clingo (answer set programming) composes candidate explanations. |
| Evidence Worker | `ewv3/` | Finds the sentences in the documents that bear on a claim and builds an evidence packet. |
| Assessor | `hera1/` | Judges each packet: supports, contradicts, or not enough information. It also approves outward requests for missing evidence. |

One closed-loop run goes like this:

1. Intake receives the incident notice and the first documents. The Lead builds the board.
2. The Specialist, Evidence Worker and Assessor jobs run, up to a job limit.
3. Requests the Assessor approved go to a **simulated custodian**, which releases the
   documents it holds. By default it is deterministic and never uses the model under
   test (`ground_truth/custodian_holdings.json`), so two models face the same world.
4. Released documents re-enter through Intake. The loop repeats until the waves run
   out or a round limit is reached.

The model proposes and judges. Python decides what a claim's status is, rejects
references to IDs that don't exist, and never lets the run mark a root cause on its
own. A missing record is treated as a gap, not as a finding.

## Ground truth and scoring

`ground_truth/` holds what runs are scored against:

- `r3_human_rca_chart.json`: a transcription of the human RCA chart for the case
  (23 cause nodes, 14 cause links, open questions and proposed solutions).
- `evidence_map_draft.json`: which sentences in E01–E16 bear on each chart node, plus
  designed traps such as passages that look relevant but settle nothing.
- `custodian_holdings.json`: which documents the simulated custodian holds and when it
  releases them.

`V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py` reports how many chart
nodes the board covers, whether the key sentences were assessed with a sensible
stance, and whether the traps were avoided. Node matching is by word overlap, so it
lists every match for you to check.

## Results so far

gpt-oss:20b on Ollama, 256 role jobs per run, fixed custodian, one run each. The
**context** column is the Ollama context window; "6k kept free" means 6,000 tokens
of it were reserved for the Specialist's reasoning and answer, with its prompt
trimmed to fit the rest.

| | Earlier fix | 16k, 6k kept free | 32k | 32k, low effort | 32k, medium effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key supporting sentences found | 3/14 | 5/14 | 5/14 | 2/14 | 3/14 |
| Key sentences assessed | 17 | 17 | 19 | 17 | 20 |
| Documents used | 14 | 14 | 16 | 14 | 15 |
| Overclaimed sentences | 5 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| Claims on the board | 24 | 35 | 40 | 30 | 40 |
| Failed jobs | 14 | 4 | 13 | 3 | 14 |
| Cut-off answers | 41 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Run time | – | ~3¾ h | ~5⅓ h | ~1¾ h | ~4 h |

What this shows so far:

- Keeping room for the answer removed cut-off answers.
- A larger window let more documents reach the Specialist and cut overclaiming.
- Lower reasoning effort was faster but found less. High effort was too slow to finish
  (about 15 jobs an hour).
- **The board still rarely reaches the causes on the chart.** The Specialist only
  looks at documents through the claims already on the board, so evidence that fits
  no current claim never steers it. Directing it at one document at a time is being
  tested as the next step.

Caveats: each column is a single run, so differences of one or two may be noise.
The "supporting sentences" count is generous, because it credits a support on any
claim. Run outputs (50–110 MB each) are not in this repository.

content.text:
The system fails in three places: it never proposes claims for most of the key evidence, it never shows a supported cause chain, and jobs fail for reasons we could fix. I also found that we can't yet measure progress reliably. The numbers below come from the four recent gpt-oss runs, mostly the 32k one, which was the best.

**1. Most key evidence never becomes a claim (the biggest problem)**
- **The cause:** the Specialist only reads documents through the claims already on the board. A sentence that fits no current claim, such as "valve seeps with handle closed" or "only one keeper fitted", never steers it.
- **The result:** 5 of 14 key supporting sentences found, and 0–1 of the 23 chart nodes matched.
- **The test we ran:** pointing the Specialist at one document at a time recovered those leads. That change isn't built yet.

**2. There is never a supported cause chain**
- **Links:** the 32k board has 34 cause links, and every one is still "candidate". None was ever confirmed or rejected, so the board can't show a cause chain at all.
- **Claim types:** of the 40 claims, 19 are "unknown condition" and 17 are "component state". Only one, the beam falling, has a status. The board can't mark a component state as shown by evidence, so it can't match the chart's "observed" and "proposed" labels. That's task T10 in the goals.

**3. The board fills with weak and duplicate claims**
- **Near-duplicates:** "carrier raised before the fall" and "carrier raised at the time of the fall" are both on the board.
- **Conflicts:** two claims give different times for removing the backup rolls (06:35 and 10:20). Both stay on the board unresolved.
- **Neutral assessments:** 80 of 114 assessments, 70%, came back neutral. Many are reasonable, but they use up jobs.
- **The cap:** all this pushes the board to the 40-claim limit early.

**4. Jobs fail for fixable reasons**

| Cause | 32k run | 32k medium |
|---|---|---|
| Specialist: proposal goes over the 40-claim cap | 5 | 9 |
| Assessor: cites text outside its evidence packet | 5 | 5 |
| Evidence Worker: too many search queries | 2 | 0 |
| Assessor: invalid comparison label | 1 | 0 |

- **Late Specialist failures:** once the board hits the cap, every later Specialist job fails. That cuts off exploration exactly when the later documents arrive.
- **Assessor failures:** the claim that job covered stays unassessed.

**5. Fixed already, or ruled out**
- **Cut-off answers:** from 41 to 0, by keeping room for the answer.
- **Trimmed prompts:** none at 32k.
- **High reasoning effort:** too slow to use, at about 15 jobs an hour.

**6. We can't yet measure progress reliably**
- **A generous scorer:** it counts a support even when it lands on the wrong claim.
- **Single runs:** each setting ran once, and scores ranged from 2 to 5 of 14. A change of one or two could just be noise.
- **No measure for new claims:** claims that aren't on the chart aren't checked for whether they're grounded in a document.
- **Untested goal:** order independence (G5) has never been tested.

**The order I'd suggest**
1. Fix the scorer. It needs no model and lets us re-score the old runs.
2. Raise the claim cap, and stop the Assessor citing outside its packet. Both are cheap fixes that cut the failures.
3. Add the one-document-per-job Specialist change.
4. Make cause links get assessed, so a supported chain can appear.
