tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache [REDACTED] inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

**What goes wrong:**
- **It mostly says "none".** About 30 claims got no node at all, including clear ones:
  - "valve IV-RB3-17 was closed during outage" (G02);
  - "carrier reached upper travel limit" (G06);
  - "keeper plate engaged with link arm" (G03);

  - "valve closed or sealed" got G04 opposite and G09, instead of G02 part and G13 opposite;

  - "moved beyond the support envelope" got G01 and G08 instead of G10.
- **Thinking on doesn't rescue it.** It agreed on only 5 of the 13 claims it answered before it crashed, and it kept adding G13 to pressure claims.

# Claim-to-node labels: review

Draft by Claude, 2026-11-11. Correct the **Nodes** column in `claim_node_labels.json` (the scorer reads that file, not this one).
Fit: **same** = the claim states the node; **part** = it states part of it or one instance; **opposite** = it denies it. Blank = no chart node.

## Chart nodes

| ID | Text |
|---|---|
| G01 | Yoke drifted but carrier beam did not |
| G02 | R3 Backup Raise "isolated" |
| G03 | Keeper installation & location |
| G04 | No stop for carrier beam without backup rolls installed |
| G05 | Carrier beam came off of yoke with the keeper plate still intact (bolted) |
| G06 | Carrier beam wedged on mill spreader and mill posts |
| G07 | Hydraulics shut off with isolation valve slowly bleeding backwards allowing the cylinder fluid to vacate the pipe |
| G08 | carrier beam shifted off of yoke when stored in the upright position due to being wedge against mill beam housing with no "stops" or back up rolls installed |
| G09 | NO mechanism to prevent carrier beams from being wedged |
| G10 | carrier beam shifted |
| G11 | Excess Clearance????? Measurements do not allow for clearance to get over the yoke "in resting position" |
| G12 | Original Mill Design |
| G13 | R3 Hydraulic Isolation valve has slow bleed through |
| G14 | Isolation valves are not routinely inspected but rather replaced when found defective |
| G15 | J. Tessling "not required" |
| G16 | R3 LOTO- Task Specific Procedure "Stripper Box Changeout" |
| G17 | Stored Energy not accounted for "A" hydraulics |
| G18 | All energy sources (gravity) not accounted for during isolation for task |
| G19 | Only one keeper installed |
| G20 | Original Mill Design (keeper) |
| G21 | Original Mill Design (no stop) |
      86 ground_truth/claim_node_labels_REVIEW.md

    def test_unassessed_key_sentences_lower_recall(self):
        out = sat.score(report([], []), TRUTH)
        self.assertEqual(out["key_sentences_assessed"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(out["key_sentence_recall"], 0.0)


def labelled(fits_by_text, source="human"):
    labels = {sat.normalise(text): {"source": source, "nodes": [{"id": n, "fit": f} for n, f in fits]}
              for text, fits in fits_by_text.items()}
    return {**TRUTH, "labels": labels}


class Labels(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_label_matches_a_claim_that_shares_too_few_words(self):
        c = claim("C1", "Valve IV-RB3-17 was not properly sealed")
        truth = labelled({"Valve IV-RB3-17 was not properly sealed": [("G13", "same")]})
        out = sat.score(report([c], [assess("C1", "m8", SEEPAGE, "supports")]), truth)
        self.assertTrue(out["node_matches"]["G13"]["covered"])
        self.assertEqual((out["supports_found"], out["claim_matching"]), (1, {"human": 1}))

    def test_a_label_of_no_node_overrides_word_overlap(self):
        c = claim("C1", "Hydraulic isolation valve has slow bleed through")
        out = sat.score(report([c], []), labelled({c["text"]: []}))
        self.assertFalse(out["node_matches"]["G13"]["covered"])
        self.assertEqual(out["claims_off_chart"], 1)

# Root Cause Analysis with cooperating LLM roles

A research harness for building an incident root cause analysis (RCA) from documents,
using five cooperating roles driven by a local or hosted language model. It is tested
on one synthetic industrial incident and scored against a human-made RCA chart for
that incident.

The question it studies: can a model, split into bounded roles with Python checks
between them, keep investigating as documents arrive at any time, check each document
against every claim, ask for missing evidence, and build an RCA board without
declaring a root cause the evidence does not support?

This is research code (v0.4). It is not a product, and the results below come from
single runs on one case.

## The test case

**R3 carrier beam fall.** A raised delivery carrier beam on a rolling-mill roughing
stand fell into the mill pit and struck an equipment sled and a temporary scaffold.
Nobody was hurt. The case has 16 documents (E01–E16): the incident notice, functional
descriptions, inspection notes, test results, logs and statements. All of them are
synthetic research fixtures, not real company records.

Documents arrive in waves: some with the incident, some only when the system asks for
them, and some unprompted.

## How it works

| Role | Package | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | `piris/` | Registers each arriving document, extracts and indexes its text, and links replies to the request that asked for them. It does not judge evidence. |
| Lead | `cferp/` | Keeps the investigation board (claims, causal links, requests, open needs), queues work for the other roles, and redoes only the work a new document affects. |
| Specialist | `sahs/` | Proposes candidate causes and mechanisms as typed propositions and rules. Python validates them, and Clingo (answer set programming) composes candidate explanations. |
| Evidence Worker | `ewv3/` | Finds the sentences in the documents that bear on a claim and builds an evidence packet. |
| Assessor | `hera1/` | Judges each packet: supports, contradicts, or not enough information. It also approves outward requests for missing evidence. |

One closed-loop run goes like this:

1. Intake receives the incident notice and the first documents. The Lead builds the board.
2. The Specialist, Evidence Worker and Assessor jobs run, up to a job limit.
3. Requests the Assessor approved go to a **simulated custodian**, which releases the
   documents it holds. By default it is deterministic and never uses the model under
   test (`ground_truth/custodian_holdings.json`), so two models face the same world.
4. Released documents re-enter through Intake. The loop repeats until the waves run
   out or a round limit is reached.

The model proposes and judges. Python decides what a claim's status is, rejects
references to IDs that don't exist, and never lets the run mark a root cause on its
own. A missing record is treated as a gap, not as a finding.

## Ground truth and scoring

`ground_truth/` holds what runs are scored against:

- `r3_human_rca_chart.json`: a transcription of the human RCA chart for the case
  (the incident plus 22 cause nodes, 22 cause-and-effect pairs, open questions and proposed solutions).
- `evidence_map_draft.json`: which sentences in E01–E16 bear on each chart node, plus
  designed traps such as passages that look relevant but settle nothing.
- `custodian_holdings.json`: which documents the simulated custodian holds and when it
  releases them.

`V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py` reports how many chart
nodes the board covers, whether the key sentences were assessed with a sensible
stance, and whether the traps were avoided. Node matching is by word overlap, so it
lists every match for you to check.

## Results so far

gpt-oss:20b on Ollama, 256 role jobs per run, fixed custodian, one run each. The
**context** column is the Ollama context window; "6k kept free" means 6,000 tokens
of it were reserved for the Specialist's reasoning and answer, with its prompt
trimmed to fit the rest.

| | Earlier fix | 16k, 6k kept free | 32k | 32k, low effort | 32k, medium effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key supporting sentences found | 3/14 | 5/14 | 5/14 | 2/14 | 3/14 |
| Key sentences assessed | 17 | 17 | 19 | 17 | 20 |
| Documents used | 14 | 14 | 16 | 14 | 15 |
| Overclaimed sentences | 5 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| Claims on the board | 24 | 35 | 40 | 30 | 40 |
| Failed jobs | 14 | 4 | 13 | 3 | 14 |
| Cut-off answers | 41 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Run time | – | ~3¾ h | ~5⅓ h | ~1¾ h | ~4 h |

What this shows so far:

- Keeping room for the answer removed cut-off answers.
- A larger window let more documents reach the Specialist and cut overclaiming.
- Lower reasoning effort was faster but found less. High effort was too slow to finish
  (about 15 jobs an hour).
- **The board still rarely reaches the causes on the chart.** The Specialist only
  looks at documents through the claims already on the board, so evidence that fits
  no current claim never steers it. Directing it at one document at a time is being
  tested as the next step.

Caveats: each column is a single run, so differences of one or two may be noise.
The "supporting sentences" count is generous, because it credits a support on any
claim. Run outputs (50–110 MB each) are not in this repository.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/` | The current five-role system, its runners, scorers and tests. [Its README](V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/README.md) covers each role in detail. |
| `V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/` | Earlier versions kept for comparison: V1 is prompt-only, V2 adds research-inspired methods and rules. They share one codebase and are selected by profile (see [VERSION_GUIDE.md](V1_V2_Prompt_and_Rules/source/RCA_Version_Labeled_Codebase/VERSION_GUIDE.md)). The R3 documents live in its test fixtures. |
| `ground_truth/` | The human RCA chart, the evidence map and the custodian holdings. |
| `scripts/` | Launchers that run V1, V2 and V3 on the same case. |
| `tests_ollama/` | Tests for the Ollama client. |

## Setup

Tested with Python 3.13. Clingo is the only V3 dependency:

```bash
python -m pip install -r V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/requirements-sahs.txt
```

For local models, install [Ollama](https://ollama.com) and pull a model first, for
example `ollama pull gpt-oss:20b`. For hosted models, set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in your
shell. See `.env.example` in the V1/V2 codebase; never commit a real key.

## Run

All commands run from the repository root.

One closed-loop run on a local model:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_v3_closed_loop.py \
  --provider ollama_native --model gpt-oss:20b \
  --num-ctx 32768 --answer-reserve 6000 \
  --max-jobs 256 --call-timeout 600 \
  --output outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

Several runs of one configuration, with the spread between them:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/run_repeats.py \
  --provider ollama_native --model gpt-oss:20b --runs 3 \
  --num-ctx 32768 --answer-reserve 6000 \
  --output-prefix outputs/gptoss_32k
```

Score a run against the ground truth, and check its workflow health:

```bash
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_against_truth.py outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
python V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired/scripts/score_run.py outputs/r3_closed_loop.json
```

Run the tests, which use scripted model replies and need no model:

```bash
cd V3_Neurosymbolic_Inspired
PYTHONPATH=. python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

`--help` on any script lists every option. To run V1, V2 and V3 on the same case,
use `scripts/run_r3_all_versions_live.py` (see [OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md](OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md)).

## Further reading

- [CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md](CLOSED_LOOP_RUNBOOK.md): how a run works, its output, exit codes and failures.
- [FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md](FRAMEWORK_TASK_GOALS.md): the goals (grounded, honest, responsive, asks well, order-independent, comparable) and the tasks toward them.
- [FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md](FRAMEWORK_AUDIT.md): the problems found in earlier runs.
- [RESEARCH_BRIEF.md](RESEARCH_BRIEF.md): related research for each problem.
- [OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md](OLLAMA_ADAPTER.md): the native Ollama client.
- `CHANGELOG_v0.2.md` to `CHANGELOG_v0.4.md`: version history.

content.text:
I labelled every claim myself: all 205 distinct claims from the eight saved runs, using the same rules as the first 50. That fits the comparison, since I'm not the model under test (gpt-oss:20b), so the pipeline is still all one model and the scoring stays independent of it. The one cost: labels are only as good as my reading until you review them.

**Labelling rules:**
- A question about something ("it is uncertain whether…") counts as part of that node.
- A denial is marked "opposite".
- Claims about records, sensors, handover or coordination match no node, because the chart has none for them.

**Re-scored with full labels:**

| Run | Nodes stated | Key supports on the right claim | Supports on any claim | Supports on a claim denying the node | Edges with both ends on the board |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 8 | 1/14 | 3 | 0 | 5 |
| fix2 | 7 | 3/14 | 3 | 0 | 4 |
| fix3 | 7 | 2/14 | 3 | 0 | 5 |
| retrievalfix | 5 | 1/14 | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| 16k | 7 | 2/14 | 5 | 1 | 3 |
| 32k | 8 | 3/14 | 5 | 2 | 4 |
| 32k low | 11 | 2/14 | 2 | 0 | 11 |
| 32k medium | 10 | 1/14 | 3 | 0 | 6 |

"Nodes stated" counts chart nodes that at least one board claim puts forward, whether or not evidence supports it.

**What this shows:**
- **The board finds more of the chart than word overlap said:** 5 to 11 nodes per run, not 0 to 7. The nodes it keeps finding are:
  - G02 (valve isolated)
  - G04 (no stop with the rolls out)
  - G07 (hydraulics lost)
  - G06 and G08 (carrier wedged or stored raised)
- **The board rarely gets those nodes supported:** at most 3 of the 14 key supporting sentences landed on the right claim in any run. That points at the gaps Step 1 targets: claim status never changes, and evidence is matched to claims loosely.
- **Rarely stated:**
  - G13, the valve bleeding through, the actual mechanism: 3 runs.
  - G18, gravity not accounted for: 4 runs.
  - G14, G15, G19 and G20–G22: never. Most of these have no evidence in the documents at all.

**Changes, all uncommitted:**
- `ground_truth/claim_node_labels.json` now holds 205 labels, marked as my draft.
- `ground_truth/claim_node_labels_REVIEW.md` lists them all, grouped by node, with a reason for each.
- `score_against_truth.py --unlabelled` lists any claim a new run produces that has no label, so I can label it before scoring.
- I added one test; all 445 pass.
- I updated the README's scoring paragraph to match.

The calls most worth checking in the review file:
- I treated "pit opening restricted by scaffold or sled" as denying G04 (a stop existed).
- I mapped "no sealing test or pressure check on the isolated side" to G17 (stored energy not accounted for).

content.content:
## Step 1: a status for every claim and link (Gap 1)

A new deterministic module in the Lead (`cferp/status.py`). It reruns after every
committed result and records its output as an event.

**A support must cover the whole claim.** Many claims join several facts, such as "Valve
IV-RB3-17 was isolated at 11:10". A passage can support one part (the B supply was
isolated at 11:10) and leave another open (that this valve was the one). So:

- **Parts are fixed when the claim is made.** The Specialist lists a claim's parts when it proposes it, for example `valve IV-RB3-17` / `was isolated` / `at 11:10`. Python checks that each part is a phrase from the claim, and that together they cover all of it.
- **The Assessor marks parts.** For each passage, it says which of those listed parts the passage supports, contradicts or leaves open. Because the list is fixed, assessments from different passages can be combined.
- **Status follows the parts.** A claim is `shown` only when every part is shown, by one passage or several. Otherwise it is `partly shown`.
- **Missing parts become needs.** Each part still missing becomes a need automatically, so the next search targets what's missing.

**The Assessor's answers become** `supports`, `consistent_with`, `insufficient`,
`not_relevant`, `weakens`, `contradicts`, replacing the single `neutral`:
- **`consistent_with`:** the passage fits the claim but doesn't show it.
- **`insufficient`:** the passage bears on the claim but can't settle it. This includes a record saying something wasn't measured or can't be told.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Show the status of every claim and link on a saved run's board, and its causal chains.

Uses the same rules as the Lead (``cferp/status.py``) and needs no model. Boards from
before v0.5 have no claim parts, no origin records and only ``neutral`` for passages
that settle nothing, so each claim reads as one part, each document as its own source,
and ``neutral`` as ``open``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from collections import Counter
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from cferp.status import board_status  # noqa: E402


def render(report: dict, view: dict, max_paths: int) -> str:
    texts = {c["claim_id"]: c.get("text", "") for c in report["board"]["claims"]}
    docs = {m["material_id"]: m.get("title", m["material_id"]).removesuffix(".md")
            for m in report["board"].get("materials", ())}
    out = [f"claims by status: {view['claims_by_status']}", f"links by status:  {view['links_by_status']}", ""]
    order = ["reported", "shown", "partly shown", "contested", "contradicted", "open", "unchecked"]
    for status in order:
        rows = [r for r in view["claims"].values() if r["status"] == status]
        if not rows:
            continue
        out.append(f"{status.upper()} ({len(rows)})")
        for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["claim_id"]):
            src = sorted({docs.get(s, s) for p in r["parts"] for s in p["support_sources"]})
            con = sorted({docs.get(s, s) for p in r["parts"] for s in p["contradict_sources"]})
            extra = (f" supports {','.join(src)}" if src else "") + (f" contradicts {','.join(con)}" if con else "")
            out.append(f"  {r['claim_id']}: {texts.get(r['claim_id'], '')[:90]}{extra}  {r['assessments_by_effect']}")
        out.append("")
    chains = view["chains"]
    paths = chains["paths"]
    out.append(f"CHAINS: {len(paths)} paths from the incident{' (truncated)' if chains['truncated'] else ''}; "
               f"{len(chains['claims_on_no_path'])} claims on no path")
    out.append(f"  weakest claim on each path: {dict(Counter(p['weakest_claim']['status'] for p in paths))}")
    for p in paths[:max_paths]:
        claims = [i for k, i in p["steps"] if k == "claim"]
        statuses = [s for (k, _), s in zip(p["steps"], p["statuses"]) if k == "claim"]
        out.append("  " + " <- ".join(f"{c}[{s}]" for c, s in zip(claims, statuses)))
    if chains["claims_on_no_path"]:
        out.append("  on no path: " + ", ".join(chains["claims_on_no_path"]))
    return "\n".join(out)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("run", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")

content.text:
The first part of Step 1 works: Python now works out every claim's and link's status, and I've run it on the saved 32k board. That run shows the status rules are fine, but many of the Assessor's answers they rely on are wrong.

**What I built:**
- **`cferp/status.py`:** the status rules from the plan, worked out fresh from the board each time with no model.
  - Claim statuses are shown, partly shown, contested, contradicted, open and unchecked; the incident claim stays "reported".
  - Each claim is split into parts, and missing parts are listed. Old boards have no parts, so each claim counts as one part.
  - A support counts once per original source, so a recap and the record it was prepared from count as one.
  - Links are "proposed", or "both ends shown" when both their claims are shown.
  - The chain view follows links back from the incident and names the weakest point on each path.
- **Rule I settled myself:** a claim with one contradicted part counts as contradicted, even when its other parts are supported. A claim joins its parts with "and", so one false part makes it false. The plan's table didn't cover that case.
- **`scripts/board_status.py RUN.json`:** prints the status view of any saved run.
- **Tests:** 19 new; the full suite of 464 passes. I added the first-check results below to `DESIGN_PLAN_v0_5.md`.

**What the 32k board looks like:**
- **Claims:**
  - 5 shown
  - 7 contested
  - 3 contradicted
  - 1 open
  - 23 unchecked, never assessed at all
- **Links:** 34 in all; 4 have both ends shown.
- **Chains:** 15 paths lead back from the incident, and 24 claims are on none. Many of those 24 are near-duplicates, such as four versions of "keeper bolted at the fall".
- **The path that matters most:** fall ← pressure drop ← "valve not closed", and the last claim is contradicted. That is the right weak point to flag: the true cause is a closed valve that bled through (G13), and the board never proposed it.

**Where the Assessor's answers are wrong:**
- **Absence read as support:** "No branch hydraulic pressure is visible" was taken as showing the pressure dropped.
- **A misreading:** "examination was carried out after removal" was taken as contradicting "backup rolls were removed".
- **Traps working:**
  - E13, the replacement configuration, contradicts "keeper bolted";
  - E16, the recap, contradicts "valve status unknown".
- **A passage supporting opposite claims:** E05 and E12 support both "raised at the fall" and "not raised at the fall".

The new answer options in the plan (`insufficient`, `not_relevant`, marking parts of a claim) target the first two. For the last one I added a check to the plan: when the Specialist proposes a claim that denies another, the pair is recorded, and Python flags any passage that supports both.

The Lead doesn't use these statuses yet, so they don't steer any work.

**The two options for the next part of Step 1:**
- **Assessor answers first (my pick):** the new answer options, parts and the denial pairs. Statuses are only as good as the answers behind them, so this comes first.
- **Wire status into the Lead:** record a status event after each result and turn missing parts into needs.

content.content:
"""JSON Schemas for HERA model replies, for providers with structured output.

Field names and enums mirror ``validate_statement_batch``,
``validate_comparison`` and the request-review checks in ``Hera1Engine``. A schema constrains the reply's shape only; those
validators still decide whether a quote is located in the packet, whether
statement IDs resolve, and what a finding may claim.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

STATEMENT_KINDS = ["incident_observation", "reported_event", "incident_causal_statement",
                   "general_mechanism", "procedure", "hypothetical", "other"]
STATEMENT_MODALITIES = ["asserted", "reported", "measured", "conditional", "possible",
                        "negated", "inferred", "unclear"]
FINDING_RELATIONS = ["supports", "weakens", "contradicts", "does_not_address",
                     "insufficient_or_unclear"]
_ALIGNMENT = ["match", "mismatch", "unknown"]

_STATEMENT_FIELDS: dict[str, Any] = {
    "statement_id": {"type": "string"},
    "material_id": {"type": "string"},
    "source_id": {"type": "string"},
    "source_version": {"type": "string"},
    "representation_id": {"type": "string"},
    "quote": {"type": "string"},
    "start_offset": {"type": "integer"},
    "kind": {"enum": STATEMENT_KINDS},
    "modality": {"enum": STATEMENT_MODALITIES},
    "scope": {"type": "string"},
    "timing": {"type": "string"},
}

EXTRACT_STATEMENTS_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
    "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["statements"],
    "properties": {"statements": {"type": "array", "items": {
        "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
        "required": list(_STATEMENT_FIELDS), "properties": _STATEMENT_FIELDS,
    }}},
}

def validate_comparison(raw: dict[str, Any], task: AssessmentTask, statements: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    _only_keys(raw, {"parts"}, "comparison")
    parts = raw.get("parts")
    expected = {p["part_id"] for p in task.hypothesis["parts"]}
    if not isinstance(parts, list) or len(parts) != len(expected):
        raise ModelOutputError("comparison must return each hypothesis part exactly once")
    allowed = {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts", "does_not_address", "insufficient_or_unclear"}
    known_statement_ids = {s["statement_id"] for s in statements}
    for part in parts:
        if not isinstance(part, dict):
            raise ModelOutputError("comparison part must be an object")
        _only_keys(part, {"part_id", "findings"}, "comparison part")
        findings = part.get("findings")
        if part.get("part_id") not in expected or not isinstance(findings, list) or not findings or len(findings) > 16:
            raise ModelOutputError("comparison part requires a bounded nonempty findings array")
        for finding in findings:
            if not isinstance(finding, dict):
                raise ModelOutputError("comparison finding must be an object")
            _only_keys(finding, {"relation", "statement_ids", "rationale", "inference_bridge",
                                 "relevance_status", "scope_alignment", "time_alignment"}, "comparison finding")
            refs = finding.get("statement_ids")
            if (finding.get("relation") not in allowed
                    or not isinstance(refs, list) or any(not isinstance(ref, str) for ref in refs)
                    or not set(refs).issubset(known_statement_ids)):
                raise ModelOutputError("comparison finding has invalid relation or statement reference")
            if finding["relation"] in {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts"} and not refs:
                raise ModelOutputError("impactful finding requires at least one linked source statement")
            if (not isinstance(finding.get("rationale"), str) or not finding["rationale"].strip()
                    or not isinstance(finding.get("inference_bridge"), str)):
                raise ModelOutputError("comparison rationale and inference_bridge must be text")
            if finding.get("relevance_status") not in {"direct", "indirect", "unrelated", "uncertain"}:
                raise ModelOutputError("comparison relevance_status is invalid")
            if finding["relation"] in {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts"} and not finding["inference_bridge"].strip():
                raise ModelOutputError("impactful finding requires an explicit claim-to-source inference bridge")
            for alignment in ("scope_alignment", "time_alignment"):
                if finding.get(alignment) not in {"match", "mismatch", "unknown"}:
                    raise ModelOutputError(f"comparison {alignment} must be match, mismatch, or unknown")
    ids = [p["part_id"] for p in parts]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)) or set(ids) != expected:
        raise ModelOutputError("comparison part IDs must cover assigned parts exactly")
    by_id = {s["statement_id"]: s for s in statements}
    part_specs = {p["part_id"]: p for p in task.hypothesis["parts"]}
    scope_flags = []
    for result in parts:
        spec = part_specs[result["part_id"]]
        seen_statement_ids = set()
        for finding_index, finding in enumerate(result["findings"]):
            linked = [by_id[sid] for sid in finding["statement_ids"]]
            if seen_statement_ids.intersection(finding["statement_ids"]):
                raise ModelOutputError("one source statement cannot be assigned to multiple findings for the same part")
            seen_statement_ids.update(finding["statement_ids"])
            if finding["relevance_status"] in {"unrelated", "uncertain"} and finding["relation"] in {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts"}:
                finding["model_relation"] = finding["relation"]
                finding["relation"] = ("does_not_address" if finding["relevance_status"] == "unrelated"
                                       else "insufficient_or_unclear")
                scope_flags.append({"part_id": result["part_id"], "finding_index": finding_index,
                                    "rule": "source_relevance_not_established"})
            if any(_clear_time_mismatch(s["quote"], spec["text"]) for s in linked):
                if finding["relation"] in {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts"}:
                    finding["model_relation"] = finding["relation"]
                    finding["relation"] = "does_not_address"
                    finding["time_alignment"] = "mismatch"
                    scope_flags.append({"part_id": result["part_id"], "finding_index": finding_index,
                                        "rule": "lexical_incident_time_mismatch"})
            if spec["claim_type"] in {"incident_fact", "incident_causal_link"}:
                reason = None
                if finding["relation"] in {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts"}:
                    allowed_kinds = ({"incident_observation", "reported_event", "incident_causal_statement"}
                                     if spec["claim_type"] == "incident_fact"
                                     else {"incident_causal_statement"})
                    if linked and any(s["kind"] not in allowed_kinds for s in linked):
                        reason = "source_type_does_not_assess_incident_claim"
                        finding["model_relation"] = finding["relation"]
                        finding["relation"] = "does_not_address"
                    elif finding["scope_alignment"] == "mismatch" or finding["time_alignment"] == "mismatch":
                        reason = "incident_scope_or_time_mismatch"
                        finding["model_relation"] = finding["relation"]
                        finding["relation"] = "does_not_address"
                    elif finding["scope_alignment"] != "match" or finding["time_alignment"] != "match":
                        reason = "incident_scope_or_time_unresolved"
                        finding["model_relation"] = finding["relation"]
                        finding["relation"] = "insufficient_or_unclear"
                    elif linked and any(s["modality"] not in {"asserted", "reported", "measured", "negated"}
                                        for s in linked):
                        reason = "source_modality_is_not_incident_observation"
                        finding["model_relation"] = finding["relation"]
                        finding["relation"] = "insufficient_or_unclear"
                if finding["relation"] == "supports":
                    allowed_kinds = ({"incident_observation", "reported_event"}
                                     if spec["claim_type"] == "incident_fact"
                                     else {"incident_causal_statement"})
                    if (not linked or any(s["kind"] not in allowed_kinds
                                          or s["modality"] not in {"asserted", "reported", "measured"}
                                          for s in linked)):
                        reason = "source_type_or_polarity_does_not_support_incident_claim"
                        finding["model_relation"] = "supports"
                        finding["relation"] = "insufficient_or_unclear"
                if reason:
                    scope_flags.append({"part_id": result["part_id"], "finding_index": finding_index,
                                        "rule": reason})
        # Retain separate findings but also provide a convenient per-part summary.
        from .lifecycle import aggregate_part_findings
        result["relation"] = aggregate_part_findings(result["findings"])
        result["statement_ids"] = list(dict.fromkeys(
            sid for finding in result["findings"] for sid in finding["statement_ids"]))
    return parts, scope_flags

import unittest

from ewv3.contracts import (CandidateLink, EvidenceWorkerResult, SearchPassStatus,
                            SlotResult, WorkPhase)
from sahs.engine_contracts import CandidateExplanation, CausalGraph, SpecialistResult

from hera1 import (
    AssessmentRoute, AssessmentTask, EvidenceMaterial, Hera1Engine, HeraPipelineAdapter,
    InMemoryAssessmentLedger, VersionSnapshot,
)


class ScriptedModel:
    def __init__(self, responses):
        self.responses = list(responses)
        self.calls = []

    def ask(self, task, system, payload):
        self.calls.append((task, system, payload))
        return self.responses.pop(0)


class FixedVersions:
    def __init__(self, snapshot_id="case:s1", board="b1", versions=None):
        self.snapshot_id = snapshot_id
        self.board = board
        self.material_versions = versions or {"D1": "v1"}

    def read(self, case_id, material_ids):
        return VersionSnapshot(self.snapshot_id, self.board,
                               {k: v for k, v in self.material_versions.items() if k in material_ids})


def material(text="A leaking valve can cause pressure loss.", start=0):
    return EvidenceMaterial("L1", "D1", "v1", "R1", text, "manual", start,
                            {"page": 2, "candidate_link_id": "L1"})


def evidence_task(**overrides):
    data = dict(
        schema_version="1", task_id="t1", work_item_id="w1", event_id="e1",
        case_id="c1", case_snapshot_id="case:s1", board_version="b1",
        task_kind="evidence_review", sender_role="evidence_worker", sender_id="ew7",
        materials=(material(),),
        hypothesis={"hypothesis_id": "h1", "parts": [
            {"part_id": "p1", "claim_type": "incident_fact", "text": "The valve leaked during the event."},
            {"part_id": "p2", "claim_type": "incident_causal_link", "text": "The leak caused pressure loss."},
        ]},
    )
    data.update(overrides)
    return AssessmentTask(**data)


def extraction(quote="A leaking valve can cause pressure loss.", kind="general_mechanism", modality="conditional"):
    return {"statements": [{"statement_id": "s1", "material_id": "L1", "source_id": "D1",
                            "source_version": "v1", "representation_id": "R1", "quote": quote,
                            "start_offset": 0, "kind": kind, "modality": modality,
                            "scope": "general", "timing": "unspecified"}]}


def comparison(second="supports"):
    return {"parts": [
        {"part_id": "p1", "findings": [finding("does_not_address", ["s1"], "No incident occurrence is stated.")]},
        {"part_id": "p2", "findings": [finding(second, ["s1"], "The source describes a possible mechanism.")]},
    ]}


def finding(relation, statement_ids, rationale, scope="match", timing="match", relevance="direct"):
    bridge = rationale if relation in {"supports", "weakens", "contradicts"} else ""
    return {"relation": relation, "statement_ids": statement_ids, "rationale": rationale,
            "inference_bridge": bridge, "relevance_status": relevance,
            "scope_alignment": scope, "time_alignment": timing}

def test_invalid_source_quote_fails_assessment_and_routes_to_lead(self):
        model = ScriptedModel([extraction("not in source")])
        result = Hera1Engine(model, FixedVersions()).run(evidence_task())
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "assessment_failed")
        self.assertEqual(result.destination_role, "lead")
        self.assertEqual(result.model_calls, 1)

    def test_negated_incident_statement_cannot_support_positive_event(self):
        text = "The valve did not leak during the incident."
        task = evidence_task(materials=(EvidenceMaterial("L1", "D1", "v1", "R1", text),))
        output = {"parts": [
            {"part_id": "p1", "findings": [finding("supports", ["s1"], "The passage mentions the leak.")]},
            {"part_id": "p2", "findings": [finding("does_not_address", ["s1"], "No causal link is stated.")]},
        ]}
        model = ScriptedModel([
            {"statements": [{"statement_id": "s1", "material_id": "L1", "source_id": "D1",
                "source_version": "v1", "representation_id": "R1", "quote": text, "start_offset": 0,
                "kind": "incident_observation", "modality": "negated", "scope": "incident", "timing": "incident"}]},
            output,
        ])
        result = Hera1Engine(model, FixedVersions()).run(task)
        finding_out = result.payload["parts"][0]["findings"][0]
        self.assertEqual(finding_out["model_relation"], "supports")
        self.assertEqual(finding_out["relation"], "insufficient_or_unclear")

    def test_wrong_time_or_scope_cannot_support_incident_claim(self):
        text = "The valve leaked during the previous shift."
        task = evidence_task(materials=(EvidenceMaterial("L1", "D1", "v1", "R1", text),))
        model = ScriptedModel([
            {"statements": [{"statement_id": "s1", "material_id": "L1", "source_id": "D1",
                "source_version": "v1", "representation_id": "R1", "quote": text, "start_offset": 0,
                "kind": "incident_observation", "modality": "reported", "scope": "previous shift", "timing": "previous shift"}]},
            {"parts": [
                {"part_id": "p1", "findings": [finding("supports", ["s1"], "Leak is reported.", scope="mismatch", timing="mismatch")]},
                {"part_id": "p2", "findings": [finding("does_not_address", ["s1"], "No causal link.")]},
            ]},
        ])
        result = Hera1Engine(model, FixedVersions()).run(task)
        self.assertEqual(result.payload["parts"][0]["relation"], "does_not_address")
        self.assertIn(result.payload["scope_guard_flags"][0]["rule"],
                      {"incident_scope_or_time_mismatch", "lexical_incident_time_mismatch"})

    def test_procedure_statement_cannot_support_that_an_event_occurred(self):
        text = "Valve V-7 must be isolated before maintenance."
        task = evidence_task(materials=(EvidenceMaterial("L1", "D1", "v1", "R1", text),))

                "source_version": "v1", "representation_id": "R1", "quote": text, "start_offset": 0,

            ]},
        ])
        result = Hera1Engine(model, FixedVersions()).run(task)
        self.assertEqual(result.payload["parts"][0]["relation"], "does_not_address")

    def test_lexical_negation_overrides_model_asserted_modality(self):

The Assessor part of Step 1 is done and tested with scripted model replies. It hasn't been run against a real model yet. Following your order, I'm doing each role first and the Lead last, and I've saved that as a memory.

**Already in place:** the Assessor already judges a claim in parts, and already answered with five options: supports, weakens, contradicts, does_not_address and insufficient_or_unclear. The Lead folds the last two into one "neutral" and always sends the whole claim as a single part. So most of the "neutral split" is a Lead job; the Assessor needed less change than planned.

**What I changed in `hera1/`:**
- **New answer `consistent_with`:** the passage fits the claim but doesn't show it. Like a support, it must cite a statement and give a sentence saying how it bears on the claim.
- **Absence-of-record rule:** Python marks a quote as `not_recorded` when it says something was not recorded, not visible, not measured or can't be told.
  - Such a quote can't support or contradict a claim unless the claim is itself about records. It becomes `insufficient_or_unclear` with a flag.
  - This catches the 32k error where "No branch hydraulic pressure is visible" supported "pressure dropped".
  - I checked the patterns against the ground truth. "No gross fracture … was recorded" is a support for G05 there, because an inspection that looks for fractures and records none is evidence. So I narrowed the rule to leave such inspection findings alone.
- **IDs taken from the packet:** the "cited material outside the assigned packet" failures (5–6 per run) were most likely the model miscopying the long hash IDs it repeats for every quote. The failed replies weren't saved, so I couldn't confirm that.
  - Python now takes the IDs from the packet when exactly one packet document contains the quote.
  - A quote that isn't in the packet still fails.
- **Prompt:** it now defines each answer and says to judge each part of a claim only on what that part states. It also says a record of a different object or configuration isn't about the claim, which is the E13 trap. That last point is only guidance; Python doesn't enforce it.

"""Replaceable proposal generator port and validated batch container."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Protocol

from .engine_contracts import (
    CausalRuleCandidate,
    ClarificationItem,
    InformationGap,
    Proposition,
    RejectedFragment,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ProposalRequest:
    assignment_id: str
    task_mode: str
    operation_goal: str
    target_proposition_id: str | None
    context: dict[str, Any]
    # What was left out of ``context`` to fit the prompt budget, item by item.
    omitted: tuple[str, ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ProposalBatch:
    schema_version: str
    proposed_propositions: tuple[Proposition, ...]
    proposed_rules: tuple[CausalRuleCandidate, ...]
    clarification_items: tuple[ClarificationItem, ...]
    information_gaps: tuple[InformationGap, ...]
    rejected_fragments: tuple[RejectedFragment, ...] = ()


class ProposalGenerator(Protocol):
    def propose(self, request: ProposalRequest) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


class OpenAICompatibleProposalGenerator:
    """Adapt a model exposing ask(task, system, payload) to the SAHS port."""

    def __init__(self, model: Any, system_prompt: str | None = None) -> None:
        from .prompt_builder import SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS
        if not callable(getattr(model, "ask", None)):
            raise TypeError("model must expose ask(task, system, payload)")
        self.model = model
        self.system_prompt = system_prompt or SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS
        self.calls_made = 0

    def propose(self, request: ProposalRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result = self.model.ask("sahs_proposal", self.system_prompt, request.context)
        self.calls_made += 1
        if not isinstance(result, dict):
            raise ValueError("model returned a non-object SAHS proposal")
        return result
"""Versioned, immutable history records used by SAHS state management.

These records describe Specialist workflow state only. They are not evidence
verdicts and must not be used as a substitute for the shared investigation
board maintained by the Lead.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Optional


class CandidateOperation(StrEnum):
    CREATE = "create"
    REVISE = "revise"
    SUPERSEDE = "supersede"
    REOPEN = "reopen"
    UNCHANGED = "unchanged"
    PARK = "park"
    MERGE = "merge"


class CandidateStatus(StrEnum):
    ACTIVE = "active"
    PARKED = "parked"
    SUPERSEDED = "superseded"


class FrontierAction(StrEnum):
    WAIT = "wait"
    EXPAND = "expand"
    DEFER = "defer"
    PARK = "park"
    REOPEN = "reopen"
    REOPEN_AND_EXPAND = "reopen_and_expand"


class InformationNeedStatus(StrEnum):
    PROPOSED = "proposed"
    PENDING = "pending"
    ANSWERED = "answered"
    CLOSED = "closed"
    SUPERSEDED = "superseded"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CandidateLineage:
    candidate_id: str
    parent_candidate_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    revision: int = 1
    dependent_proposition_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    dependent_rule_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    assumption_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    dependent_annotation_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    dependent_source_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    dependent_information_need_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    dependent_clarification_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    status: CandidateStatus = CandidateStatus.ACTIVE
    last_operation: CandidateOperation = CandidateOperation.CREATE
    content_fingerprint: Optional[str] = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.candidate_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("candidate_id must be non-empty")
        if self.revision < 1:
            raise ValueError("revision must be at least 1")
        if self.candidate_id in self.parent_candidate_ids:
            raise ValueError("candidate cannot be its own parent")

    @property
    def dependency_ids(self) -> frozenset[str]:
        return (
            self.dependent_proposition_ids
            | self.dependent_rule_ids
            | self.assumption_ids
            | self.dependent_annotation_ids
            | self.dependent_source_ids
            | self.dependent_information_need_ids
            | self.dependent_clarification_ids
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class FrontierHistory:
    frontier_id: str
    target_proposition_id: str
    candidate_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    expanded_before: bool = False
    last_attempt_id: Optional[str] = None
    last_attempt_outcome: Optional[str] = None
    dependency_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    linked_need_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    last_direction_fingerprint: Optional[str] = None
    attempted_direction_fingerprints: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    workflow_status: str = "open"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class InformationNeedHistory:
    need_id: str

class ProposalGenerator(Protocol):
